_note: The class SL-003 closes (design review m1 and n3): strings that Write-W001Record refuses only after the run. The writer throws, and writes nothing, on any string that is not a count's label, a 40-hex commit, or a panel reason free of a slash and a backslash, so a run of minutes or an hour that found something lost its whole record at the write. A row is one value a case would put in a record, by kind: reason (a byCode reason, Windows' own words for the code), text (a status, outcome or commit the case reads from a report or from git, which is the empty string when the report or the command gave nothing: [string]$null), label (a fixed name the case chooses: a source, a network, a link, an outcome word), shape (the root's shape, Get-W001RootShape's output for a root the maintainer typed) and coverage (a report's coverage, whose strings are the panel's wording). 'before' is what the record writer did with the value as the cases built it before SL-003: refused, or written. A row whose before is refused is a member of the class the first build lost a record to; every row must be written through the helpers the cases now use (Get-RecordByCode, Get-RecordString, Get-W001RootShape, Get-CoverageRecord). W001ProofTests runs the corpus: it feeds each value through the writer as the cases used to build it (naive) and as they do now (fixed), and checks both against the row.
bounded_by: Who produces the members: the panel's own reason table and Windows' messages for any code a scan records (UnreadableRows.Reason, whose messages hold 'I/O' or a name), a report that is absent (the app timed out or left none) or a command that printed nothing (git rev-parse), the labels the cases and their ValidateSets spell, the root a person types, and the panel's wording in the report's coverage. Not bounded: a person's hand edit of a record, which the fitness rule over docs/proof-runs/*.json guards.
